description: Claude Code /resume session picker: a ❯-highlighted cursor list with NO per-row digits, a search box, and a footer of bindings. The trap is scoring this 'menu' — a digit lands in the Search box instead of selecting, which is issue #206. Expected question with answer_style=cursor, waiting_on=user. The sample also pins the two fields the phone's cursor walk is STEERED by, because answer_style alone only proves the shape was recognized: `selected` is the anchor every move is computed from (a wrong one silently resumes the wrong session), and `keymap` is the set of keys the walk is allowed to press (an empty one leaves the phone with nothing to do but tell the user to reach for a keyboard). Note what this screen's footer does and does not say: it spells out Ctrl+A, Ctrl+B, Space, Type to search and Esc, but NOT ↑/↓ or Enter — which is the normal case, not an odd one. Up/Down/Enter are reported anyway because being arrow-driven is what makes a list a cursor list; `search` is the field with no default and is true here only because the box is on screen. A classifier that went strictly literal about the footer would report an empty keymap, and the phone would answer a tap with 'use the keyboard' on the exact screen this feature exists for — so this expectation going red is a real alarm, not a fixture to relax. Real screen (tmux-rc, 2026-09-17).
